title: Tally
sub: Get paid today for what your agents will earn tomorrow.
say: Hello, and thank you for watching. This is Tally. Get paid today for what your agents will earn tomorrow.

title: Agents earn slowly, but pay up front
items: Agents have no credit score or collateral
Lenders cannot verify an agent's income
DeFi loans need money locked up first
say: AI agents now sell services to other agents. Each sale is small, and the money arrives over weeks, but the costs for compute, data and gas come up front. An agent cannot borrow, because it has no credit history and no collateral. A lender cannot verify its income. And DeFi lending asks for deposits that a young agent business does not have.

title: Four steps. Repaid first.
items: Payments route into a vault-controlled collector
An underwriter reads the payment history
The vault pays an advance from the pool
Later payments repay the pool first
say: Tally is receivables financing for agents. A seller sells on an H S P reusable mandate, and its payments are routed into a collector that the vault controls. An underwriter reads the verified payment history and proposes an advance. The vault pays it from the liquidity pool. Then every later payment repays the pool first, and the seller gets what is left.
This is Tally. Because the income lands in the vault, the seller cannot take the advance and walk away. The pool is repaid before the seller sees a cent.
The how it works page follows the money, from the buyer's signed mandate, through H S P, into the vault, and back out to the pool and the seller.

title: What you are about to see
items: A real vault contract on a local test chain
H S P is not connected yet, so payments are simulated
say: A quick note on what you are about to see. This is a real vault contract, running on a local test chain, with real advance and repayment transactions. The H S P gateway is not connected yet, so the buyer's payments are plain token transfers into the collector.

After signing in with the operator passcode, the overview shows the pool. It holds three hundred and one dollars, with a forty dollar reserve that takes losses first. The share price is slightly above one dollar, because the pool has already earned a fee.
The pool page shows where the money sits. Liquidity providers deposit into the pool, advances are lent out of it, and the reserve stands behind it as the first loss.

The seller console shows one advance. Ten dollars was advanced, and the buyer paid in two instalments. The first payment went to the pool, the second cleared the rest, and the pool earned a one dollar fee. The status is repaid, and the extra payment went to the seller.
Every order, advance and collection is written to an audit trail, with its transaction hash, and can be exported as a C S V.
The underwriter playground lets you try a decision. It scores the payment history, caps the advance, and always explains why it approved, reduced or declined.
